no_dt_comparison: docs/reviews/P4.4.md section 8.6 binds until P4.3 has run: the DT is prompted at a target its own P4 review showed is not its best, so no DT-versus-baseline sentence and no DT arm appears in this task

null_bound.behaviour_spread_source: mean held-out ATT of the two worst behaviour checkpoints minus that of the two best, from the committed P4.4 measurement; not re-measured here
null_bound.how_a_null_must_be_phrased: no effect larger than +/-X found, against a 3.8190 ATT spread in the behaviour policies themselves
null_bound.x_definition: max(|ci95_low|, |ci95_high|) of the decisive contrast: the largest effect the data leave standing, not the half-width around a convenient centre

pair_orientation: for i < j in arm_order, mean_difference is mean(arms[i] - arms[j]) over shared draws
per_seed_spread_role: plan section 2.3: bc_any_20 is predicted to carry the largest subset-induced variance of the three matched arms, because its draw varies in WHICH SEEDS appear as well as in which streams. Predicted before the run, not observed after it

ordering_best2_then_any_then_worst2.if_all_three_land_together: seed identity does nothing and F3's reading collapses -- learned decisively rather than from one null contrast, which is why this arm exists
ordering_best2_then_any_then_worst2.scored_by: the three cell means, strictly ordered
ordering_best2_then_any_then_worst2.statement: bc_best2_20 < bc_any_20 < bc_worst2_20 in ATT (lower is better) -- monotone in behaviour-seed quality. The mechanism claim: not 'does seed identity matter' but 'does performance TRACK behaviour-mode quality'

primary_bc_best2_20_within_delta_of_bc_t.name_when_they_disagree: consistent with equivalence, not demonstrated at this power -- reported with the CI width and NOT written up as a match
primary_bc_best2_20_within_delta_of_bc_t.statement: bc_best2_20 lands within delta of bc_top10: matched-size random sampling from the two best checkpoints reproduces %BC

registered_predictions.registered_in: docs/plans/p4.5.md section 2, committed before the first gradient step; scoring rules in section 2.1, fixed at the same commit

secondary_bc_any_20_worse_than_bc_best2_.reference_gap_note: BRIEF_13 section 3 called 2.05 the gap to the best two; section 10.1 accepted that it is the gap to the best SINGLE seed (202). Both are reported and neither is load-bearing
secondary_bc_any_20_worse_than_bc_best2_.scored_by: directional: the paired mean difference is positive and its 95% CI excludes 0. The brief gives no numeric threshold for 'comparable' and none was invented afterwards
secondary_bc_any_20_worse_than_bc_best2_.statement: bc_any_20 lands worse than bc_best2_20 by an amount comparable to the behaviour-policy gap between the best two seeds and the five-seed mixture

reused_arm.instrument_check: see gate_b, which is what makes the re-use sound
reused_arm.statement: these episodes are re-used from the merged P4.4 artifact, not re-rolled: the same model on the same draws, and re-rolling a settled number would be a second measurement of it

role: P4.5: does %BC's advantage come from WHICH behaviour checkpoints produced its training streams? Matched-size arms on the registered held-out pool, paired by draw

bc_any_20.pool: every stream of the training split
bc_any_20.role: size alone, seeds unmatched: a mixture of all five behaviour modes

bc_best2_20.role: seed identity at MATCHED SIZE: the decisive arm against bc_any_20

bc_best2_all.role: data quantity from good seeds; SECONDARY, because it is size-matched to nothing

bc_worst2_20.role: the low end of the same axis: two arms give a difference, three give an ordering

selection.declared_in: docs/plans/p4.5.md section 3, before the first gradient step

normalisation.source: the FULL training split over every dataset directory; every arm filters that same stack rather than rebuilding a dataset over its own directories

selection.role: P4.5: which streams each arm trained on, and which behaviour checkpoints produced them. The arms differ in that and in nothing else
